extractor.prompt: Extract foundational structures and founding relations in Bernet's phenomenology of the noema.
extractor.note: Partial extraction on the noema as ideal signification of a judgment (pp. 81-92). Focuses on how noematic signification is founded on punctual acts and how ideal identity emerges through synthesis.

coverage_note: Covers section 'The Noema as Ideal Signification of a Judgment' on founding relations between noetic acts and noematic significations.

units.claim: Noematic signification is more independent of the particular act than the perceived, because it is not essentially tied to the punctual act's spatiotemporal particularity.
units.quote: the said as such can be understood independently of any relation to the punctual intention of the speaker

units.claim: Ideal identity requires synthesis of identification across multiple acts; consciousness of identity presupposes this synthesis.
units.quote: consciousness of an identity presupposes a synthesis of identification
